messages:
priya: Heads-up: between 09:10-09:25 UTC we saw a coordinated ECC spike across two racks in us-west-2 (pool-gpu-7). Error rate jumped from ~0.02/card/hr to ~1.8/card/hr. Noticed a small bump in 95th latency for hosted inference routes hitting that pool. Sending logs now.
matt: saw it too, grabbing perf charts. Can you paste the raw counts? need to see XID vs ECC correctable breakdown.
priya: raw query: `SELECT time_bucket('1m', ts) as t, sum(ecc_correctable) as c FROM gpu_metrics WHERE pool='pool-gpu-7' AND ts > now() - interval '1 hour' GROUP BY t ORDER BY t;` results show a ~90s burst in rack A, then a sustained elevated baseline for 12m across rack B.
cheng: do we have affected VMs list? wondering if it's a single hw vendor / firmware batch.
priya: affected cards: hostnames: gpu-uw7-102, gpu-uw7-103, gpu-uw8-201, gpu-uw8-202. vendor labels mixed (A100-40GB mixed vendor revisions). FW versions: 52.23.x for two, 52.24.x for two.
alex: pinging infra for recent maintenance? any BIOS updates rolled out this morning?
oncall: infra change window shows a kernel driver rollout in us-west-2 at 08:40 but rollout was staged and only hit control plane nodes. No mass GPU firmware changes.
priya: SLO note: preliminary impact -> 95th gen latency up 150ms for ~15m on a small % (0.9%) of traffic because traffic was re-routed. Not critical but noisy.
matt: thresholds we currently use: auto-drain when 5 correctables/min per card sustained for 10m OR 120 correctables/hour aggregated at host. Those numbers were tuned last year for bursty noisy cards.
cheng: propose we test a tiered policy instead of binary drain: (1) signal-only alert at 1/min (2) soft-evac (deprioritize scheduling new work + migrate long jobs) at 3/min sustained 5m (3) hard-drain at 6/min sustained 3m. This gives hysteresis and reduces noisy transient replace churn.
priya: agree conceptually but need region-aware exceptions. us-west-2 is low spare capacity today; a hard-drain there would cause capacity pressure and request slowdowns. Suggest increase hard-drain threshold by 25% in regions where spare capacity < 10%.
alex: simulation idea: run our fleet-sim against last 90 days with injected spike profiles and measure SLO delta + replacement cost. I ran a quick dry-run: applied tiered policy in sim for 10k events => replacements down 42%, 95th latency delta +30ms on average.
cheng: can you paste the sim command? want to reproduce.
alex: `./fleet-sim --input events/2026-02-spikes.json --policy policies/tiered-ecc.yaml --capacity-map regions/us-west-2:0.08,regions/us-east-1:0.25 --report out.json`
priya: policy YAML snippet we discussed:
```
policy_name: tiered-ecc
tiers:
  - name: alert
    threshold: 1/min
    duration: 5m
    action: notify
  - name: soft_evacuate
    threshold: 3/min
    duration: 5m
    action: migrate_long_jobs
  - name: hard_drain
    threshold: 6/min
    duration: 3m
    action: drain_replace
region_overrides:
  low_spare: increase_thresholds: 25%
```
matt: question: how do we detect 'long jobs' vs short inference bursts? need to avoid migrating warm caches that hurt latency further.
cheng: mark jobs > 60s as long. For inference we tag requests with `session_id` TTL; we can migrate only pods with < 5 outstanding sessions. rough but works as stopgap.
oncall: we should also consider XID fatal vs ECC correctable ratio. If XID errors spike alongside ECC, escalate to emergency hardware replacement policy immediately. XIDs -> failure rate multiplier.
priya: verified: XID events were negligible in this burst (2 total), so likely correctables noise.
alex: ops cost calc from sim: with old policy we expected ~38 replace ops/month for similar workload; tiered policy sim: ~22 replaces/month. Cost saving ~42% in replacement labor + spare part usage. Latency tradeoff ~+15-35ms 95th depending on region.
matt: decision point: do we want to roll tiered policy to canary (10% of fleets) for 48h, have a kill-switch to revert? I support.
cheng: implementation notes for autodrain controller: add hysteresis window, per-region spare-capacity lookup, and XID cross-check. Also add a cooldown per-host (no more than 1 eviction/hour unless fatal).
priya: rollout plan:
- PR to add tiered policy + sim config (changeloged)
- Canary: 10% fleets in regions us-east-1 + eu-west-1 (higher spare capacity) for 48h
- Monitor: replacement count, 95/99 latency, error surface, and SLO error budget burn. Alert if replacement delta > +10% vs baseline or latency +100ms.
alex: I'll prepare sim reports and the PR. can we get infra to stand by for manual firmware rollback in us-west-2 if canary shows regressions?
oncall: infra standby OK for next 72h during business hours. add a runbook note for manual rollback steps.
matt: minor tweak: add a flag `max_evictions_per_rack_per_hour` default 2 to avoid cascade across the same rack causing power draw/thermal issues.
priya: agreed. Also adding a diagnostic job that captures `nvidia-smi -q -d ECC,UTIL` + dmesg tail and uploads to s3 on Tier2 trigger.
cheng: final: I'll author controller PR with tests and link sim outputs. If we get +1 from infra and oncall I'll merge and schedule canary.
alex: +1 to canary. I'll attach sim summary after lunch.
sre-bot: incident-note created: INCIDENT-2026-03-14-ECC-1728034567, linked to thread. Automated metrics snapshot uploaded.
priya: thanks all — summary PR expected end of day, canary tomorrow morning. :thumbsup:
